extracted.intended_audience: researchers, research managers, and research evaluators (university community)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for using bibliometric indicators and other evidence responsibly when evaluating research, and for implementing principles such as DORA and the Leiden Manifesto in university-level research assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use metrics responsibly and not in isolation
rubrics_metrics.description: Whilst bibliometric indicators can be a useful source of information when used responsibly, they are very narrow and limited measures and should not be used in isolation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine a wide range or 'basket' of contextualised metrics across a range of appropriate dimensions to supplement or inform expert, qualitative peer review and assessment. Metrics should be contextualised and not used as sole evidence for decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognise a broad range of research outputs and activities
rubrics_metrics.description: A broad range of outputs and activities should be recognised as part of any research evaluation process, not just publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This may include supervision and mentorship, openness, peer review and editorial roles, contribution to economy, society and policy, awards & honours, public engagement activities, datasets, software and creative works as well as publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fair, transparent and robust assessment procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Statement on the Responsible Use of Research Metrics in UCD identifies key principles that guide the use of research metrics including: Fair, transparent and robust research assessment procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the criteria used to evaluate research performance explicit; ensure processes are robust and transparent to those being assessed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metrics should support not supplant qualitative expert assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Research metrics will be used to support, but not supplant, qualitative expert assessment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quantitative indicators should inform and supplement expert judgement rather than replace peer review or qualitative evaluation of intrinsic research value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use Journal Impact Factor (JIF) as surrogate for individual article quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Journal Impact Factors will not be used as a surrogate measure of the quality of individual research articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DORA highlights well-documented deficiencies of JIF: citation distributions within journals are highly skewed; JIF properties are field-specific and composite across article types; JIFs can be manipulated by editorial policy; and the data used to calculate JIFs are neither transparent nor openly available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for disciplinary differences and appropriate dimensions
rubrics_metrics.description: We will take into account the many different dimensions of research, and also the variation across disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose metrics and evaluation approaches appropriate to the discipline; do not apply a one-size-fits-all indicator set across diverse fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognise career-stage, career-breaks and equality/diversity implications
rubrics_metrics.description: UCD's commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion will be evident in how we use research metrics, recognising that many factors may impact upon an individual’s research performance and/or research metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessors should consider career stage, career breaks, statutory leaves, part-time working and other protected/equality grounds when interpreting metrics and making decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer open, transparent data and beware of gaming
rubrics_metrics.description: Be aware that some metric sources (e.g., Journal Impact Factor calculations) lack transparency and can be manipulated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use transparent, auditable indicator sources where possible; be cautious of editorial or systemic practices that 'game' metrics; include caveats and requirements prior to planning evaluations (e.g., as discussed in guides like 'Using SciVal responsibly').

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt narrative CVs and qualitative evidence of impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative CVs and organisational action plans are recommended as ways to demonstrate contributions beyond venue-based metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organisations and funders are publishing guidance and action plans on developing Narrative CVs (e.g., Royal Society Résumé for Researchers, HRB Narrative CV explainer); narrative CVs allow researchers to present diverse outputs, practices and impacts for qualitative assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adhere to and implement collective reform commitments (DORA, Leiden, CoARA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Signatory commitments (e.g., DORA, Leiden Manifesto, CoARA) recognise the need to improve research assessment and set principles for measurement and reform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organisations should produce action plans to meet commitments (e.g., DORA commitments, CoARA Agreement), shift towards inclusive assessment based primarily on qualitative judgement supported by responsible quantitative indicators, and consider exemplar resources (Leiden Manifesto's 10 principles, Metric Tide report, institutional position papers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding and audit expectations for responsible assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Some funders expect organisations to commit to and demonstrate responsible assessment practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Wellcome requires organisations to publicly commit to evaluating research based on intrinsic value rather than venue and may ask organisations to show compliance as part of audits. Institutions should be prepared to document and evidence their assessment policies and practices.
